priorities.name: Enough pods/private space for call-heavy roles
priorities.issue: There aren't enough pods for associates who are on calls all day, so calls happen on the open floor and people 'camp' in the few private spaces.
whatItLooksLike: more pods are needed for associates that are on calls all day. It's a distraction for everyone else.
Lack of private spaces a lot of times because people camp in them

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (86/100 — the highest of any category at any site).
Noise & Distraction: 28 comments (68% neg); Privacy & Confidentiality: 30 comments (57% neg).

priorities.proposedAction: Assess pod/booth capacity and camping behavior against call-heavy demand; test time limits/occupancy signals before adding pods.
priorities.siteMustDo: Quantify pod demand vs. availability at peak, test anti-camping measures, and size any gap for Workplace Solutions.

priorities.name: Wi-Fi reliability on upper floors
priorities.issue: Wi-Fi on the 35th/36th floors is unreliable for calls and virtual meetings — a critical, previously-raised, still-open issue.
whatItLooksLike: Wi-Fi is a SIGNIFICANT concern. Connection at all points of the 35th and 36th Floor are not reliable for virtual conferences, phone calls, etc. This is a critical issue, which i have raised in the past, and remains unaddressed.

evidence.text: Connectivity is cited at 16% of comments vs. 11% company-wide; Technology priority score 67/100.
A named, repeatedly-raised reliability issue on specific floors — high credibility, needs escalation not re-diagnosis.

priorities.proposedAction: Escalate a floor-specific Wi-Fi coverage/capacity assessment to the Technology workstream with the prior tickets attached.
priorities.siteMustDo: Compile the history and specific locations, and drive a Technology coverage survey of floors 35–36 to closure.

priorities.name: Workstation equipment condition
priorities.issue: Equipment at desks is worn or unreliable — wires that only work in a certain position, unstable monitors, keyboards missing kickstands.
whatItLooksLike: I've been to several PulsePoints and I'm surprised at how worn some equipment is. Examples: wires that only work in a certain position, monitors that don't stay steady where you position them, keyboards that are missing their kickstands to…
problems with the equipment at desks is not uncommon

evidence.text: Hardware: 26 comments, 65% negative — a high negative rate on a maintenance-type issue.

priorities.proposedAction: Run an equipment-condition sweep and replace worn peripherals/cables on a schedule.
priorities.siteMustDo: Inventory worn equipment, replace the worst, and set a recurring refresh check.

protectWhatIsWorking.note: Maintain the current service level and monitor performance.
Maintain the current service level and monitor performance.
